clue.text: In putsch, this person is to emerge

indicators.note: the clue places the setter's self-reference within the word for a putsch, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a putsch is a coup, a sudden seizure of power
the setter speaking of themself, so ME

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will rise up during a military takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up is to surface or arise, the same as to emerge.

clue.text: Singer, one in debt, rated poorly

indicators.note: the numeral one is placed within the reshuffled pair of words
debt and rated, done poorly, come out badly arranged and must be reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone who owes money is judged harshly by a credit agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges DEBT RATED into BEARDEDTT and 'in' slips I between the last two letters. 'Singer' means a songbird here, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded tit is a small reedbed songbird, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Take away ease, we hear, for occupier

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken rather than written, so the solver writes a word sounding like it

parts.note: take away means minus, LESS; taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant is asked to give up their comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS EASE, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a lease on property, so is its tenant and occupier.

clue.text: Injury with two body parts

parts.note: the HIP and the LASH (eyelash) are both parts of the body

explanation.surface: An accident that hurt a pair of places on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplash is the neck injury caused by a sudden jolt, as in a car crash.

clue.text: British school curriculum? It's very bitter!

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the traditional basics of schooling

explanation.surface: A grumble that the British school syllabus is a harsh one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' means bitterly cold, not resentful: the answer is the shivering noise people make.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the exclamation someone makes when the weather is freezing cold.

clue.text: 9 and I squirming in seat for 730 days

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed within the word for a seat

parts.note: BUM is informal British for the backside one sits on

indicators.note: squirming letters wriggle about into a new order

parts.note: the figure 9 is written out as NINE

explanation.surface: A child wriggling on a chair, counting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squirming' turns NINE into ENNI; I joins it and 'in' sets the lot inside BUM, the British slang word for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A biennium is a period of two years, which is 2 × 365 days.

clue.text: Prod weakling, one out in white bloomers

parts.note: to prod is to poke
a weed is informal for a feeble, weedy person

explanation.surface: Someone jabs a feeble person who is outside wearing white knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers: the definition is a plant that is out in white flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Pokeweed is an American plant bearing spikes of small white flowers, so it blooms white.

clue.text: Running that may involve horse or mule or any across answer here?

definitions.text: Running that may involve horse or mule or any across answer here?

parts.words: Running that may involve horse or mule or any across answer here
parts.note: running here means smuggling; horse is slang for heroin, a mule is a courier, and every across answer contains slang for an illicit substance

explanation.surface: Racing with horses or mules, or anything else in the grid's across lights.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across answer contains drug slang: weed, herb, tea, upper, speed, acid, shrooms, kat, crack, snow, pot, coke, grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug smuggling is running narcotics across borders, often using couriers called mules.

clue.text: Disney figure liking men and women in this spot

indicators.note: the word for attraction to both sexes is placed within the word for this spot

parts.note: this spot is HERE
BI, short for bisexual, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: A cartoon character with broad tastes in romance, found right here.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbie is a car, not a person or animal, which makes 'figure' a fair stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbie is the sentient VW Beetle of Disney's The Love Bug films.

clue.text: Sign of being low-rent

definitions.meaning: a ... shed shows someone is feeling low or sad

explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop signals sadness, while a rent or rip in cloth is also a tear, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Ruining meal that's eaten cold with mixed gin

indicators.note: the cold letter is swallowed by the meal, so goes inside it

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Spoiling a cold supper by serving it with a badly mixed gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's eaten' reads as describing the meal, but it signals C going inside; 'mixed' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, so scuppering means ruining.

clue.text: A lot of depressed jockeys, those who are racing

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters jostle into a new order
a lot of a word is most but not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Many gloomy riders are among those in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts DEPRESSED to DEPRESSE, and 'jockeys' rearranges those letters. 'jockeys' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeders are people going too fast, so those who are racing along.

clue.text: Cutting papers seized by a military chief

indicators.note: the papers are grabbed and held inside the officer's title

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: A general confiscates someone's documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like an action, but is the adjective for a sharp remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidic remark is sharp and biting, which is what a cutting remark is too.

clue.text: Prism is too peculiar, having uniform properties

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun, the state of having uniform properties

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A glass prism behaves strangely, its properties the same in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges PRISM IS TOO. The definition is a phrase for the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotropism is the quality of a material whose physical properties are equal in every direction.

clue.text: This is healthy food, yet weight increases wildly

parts.note: yet and but both mean however
a ton is a unit of weight
to mushroom is to grow rapidly

explanation.surface: A dieter's lament: the food is good for you, yet the scales keep rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Button mushrooms are small young mushrooms, a low-calorie nutritious vegetable.

clue.text: Abroad, a kind of egg is not so nice

parts.note: UN is French for a, a word used abroad
Kinder eggs are chocolate eggs with a toy inside

explanation.surface: A foreign type of egg turns out less pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: A Kinder Surprise is a chocolate egg sold in Britain and Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkinder is the comparative of unkind, meaning less pleasant to others.

clue.text: Stood up before person in boat with less space

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to stand for office is to run, so stood gives RAN
a rower sits in a boat pulling oars

explanation.surface: Someone got to their feet before a cramped crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood up' looks like a single phrase, but RAN is reversed by 'up' to give NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrower means more restricted in width, so leaving less space.

clue.text: Royal hosted by Senior Dean, perhaps

indicators.note: the royal guest is put up inside the abbreviation, as a host contains a guest

parts.note: Kate, the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A princess is entertained by a senior college dean.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Dean is the British ice dancer of Torvill and Dean fame, not a college official.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean is a celebrated figure skater, so an example of a skater.

clue.text: Gee! Crossword setter's attempt at humour is tacky

parts.note: gee is the spoken name of the letter G
the setter says I'm, I am
a crack is a wisecrack, a joke

explanation.surface: The setter admits their own joke is cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes something showy but flimsy and cheap, which is what tacky means.

clue.text: Frenzied woman, European, American rebuffed

indicators.note: being rebuffed sends something back, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: a Dane is a European

explanation.surface: A wild woman from Europe is spurned by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were the wild female followers of Dionysus, known for ecstatic frenzy.

clue.text: Politician penning extravagant material

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: CON, a Conservative
OTT, over the top

explanation.surface: A politician writing something over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing; OTT (over the top) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Currently in south, one may call for a ride in winter

parts.note: currently means now
a mobile is a phone used to make calls

explanation.surface: Someone down south now phones to book transport in the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowmobile is a motor vehicle on skis used to travel over snow.

clue.text: Promoters of health spa finally stop

parts.note: WHO, the World Health Organization

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Health campaigners eventually halt a spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command to halt, used to a horse.

clue.text: Not initially rash, has success in pool?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a rash shows as spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A player who was not reckless at first manages to score at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' drops the S from SPOTS. 'Pool' is the cue game, not a swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To pot is to sink a ball into a pocket, a success in pool or snooker.

clue.text: Remove carbon from extremely dire fizzy drink

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: Coke, Coca-Cola

explanation.surface: Getting the carbon out of a terrible soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoke an engine is to clean carbon deposits from it.

clue.text: What gardener may use to sing hit

parts.note: to sing or grass is slang for informing to the police
to box is to hit with the fists

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool to accompany a hit song.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass box is the container on a lawnmower that collects cuttings.
